rule: A crossed bound is a failed leg, recorded in followup-failed-legs.json and left failing; only Carl resets one. A leg that cannot be measured (a file not supplied, a tool not installed) is NOT RUN and says why; a threshold that proves unmeasurable on supplied data fails the gate on that threshold. Amendments are recorded in this file's amendments array before any run and move no bound; a leg is added only as a NEW leg with its bound committed before its first run. The old legs, the old thresholds.json and verdict A (its narrow meaning) are untouched.
seenBeforeCommitting: the merged gate's documents and fixtures (SN_LIKELIHOOD_GATE.md sections 1 to 9, thresholds.json, results.json, oracle-results.json), including section 4's REPORTED real-sample numbers: the decided covariance's flat-case best fit 0.3470, its 68.27 percent interval 0.3238 to 0.3710 (half-width 0.0236) and DIAG's 0.3491, 0.3304 to 0.3684 (half-width 0.0190). data.mapping: the covariance rows follow the raw .dat file's order (leg I4a proves it); the sample S is the merged gate's: cal = 0 and z at least 0.01, 1,580 rows, in the pack's order (sorted by z, CID, survey), each carrying its raw-file index.
data.published: published-flat.json, held outside the repository, copied unchanged to tests/fixtures/supernova-likelihood/authentic/published-flat.json in the results commit with its sha256 in results; the printed value is read from it at run time and nothing typed.
data.sampleDifference: the stated difference of samples and analyses: the paper's constraint uses its full systematic covariance with the SH0ES calibrators in the sample; this follow-up's FULL uses the same covariance on the 1,580 Hubble-flow rows (no calibrators, z at least 0.01) and a different fitting method (a profile over a flat-case grid with an analytic offset, not the paper's sampler). The calibrators sit at z below 0.01 where the matter density has almost no leverage, and the cut removes rows, so a small difference is expected; it is allowed for only by the width of the rule below (one printed sigma), which is the size by which two estimates from nested, overlapping samples can differ. No leg is loosened for it, and a larger difference is a failed leg whose cause this PR does not claim to know.

treatments.FULL: the release's covariance block of the 1,580 rows, offset marginalised analytically exactly as the merged gate (chi2 = r^T C^-1 r - (1^T C^-1 r)^2 / (1^T C^-1 1))
treatments.DIAG: the merged gate's diagonal treatment (the pack's mu_err squared, no correlation)
treatments.SPLIT: the merged gate's decided covariance (mu_err squared on the diagonal, tau^2 = 0.02^2 between rows of one survey)
treatments.T1-n: the subset-with-block treatment: the rows named in legs U1 to U3, their exact block of FULL, the same marginalisation; planes and levels as the gate
treatments.T2-k: the low-rank projection with its retained variance: the symmetric eigendecomposition of C_F, the leading k eigenpairs (lambda_j, v_j), C_T2 = diag(r) + sum_j lambda_j v_j v_j^T with r_i = C_ii - sum_j lambda_j v_ij^2, so that the diagonal is exactly C_F's; k = 10, 30, 100 (the gate's sizes)

amendments.recorded: after run 1 of the oracle (kept as followup-run1.json: the file's integrity numbers only; it stopped at I4a by the committed rule) and before any other leg of this follow-up was computed
amendments.observed: run 1 measured: the file has the stated sha256, size and shape (I1 holds); the matrix is symmetric to 3e-8 as printed (I2, bound 1e-9, FAILS; the committed remedy, (C + C^T)/2, is what every later leg uses); it is positive definite (smallest eigenvalue 0.00080 on all 1,701 rows, 0.0052 on the 1,580-row sample; condition 460 on the sample); the rank correlation between sqrt(C_ii) and the raw file's MU_SH0ES_ERR_DIAG is 0.932 (I4a, bound 0.99, FAILS); and sqrt(C_ii) is below MU_SH0ES_ERR_DIAG on almost every row (ratio median 0.713, minimum 0.118, maximum 1.008; largest absolute difference 1.34 mag; I4b, bound 1e-5, FAILS). The decided split form's premise, that the pack's mu_err is this covariance's diagonal, is therefore false on the evidence of this file, by the amounts stated. I2, I4a and I4b stay failing.
amendments.text: By the committed rule, a failed I4a makes every later leg NOT RUN (the row mapping is unproven). I4a was written as a proxy: it assumes ERR_DIAG is the diagonal, which I4b's failure shows it is not, so it cannot tell a different diagonal from a different order. Two NEW legs, I4c and I4d, prove or refute the order from the covariance's own off-diagonal structure (supernovae observed by two surveys, and the survey blocks), by permutation tests with the bounds in their rows, committed here before they or any later leg run. If either fails, every later leg is NOT RUN and the PR says the mapping is unproven. If both pass, the later legs run in the raw file's order and carry the label 'run under AM1'. A NEW reported leg R9 records how the pack's errors differ from the file's diagonal.
amendments.verdictAM1: Two verdicts are recorded, never one in place of the other. (1) The committed function, applied to the rows as committed: because I4a fails it gives FC, and by the committed rule the downstream rows would be NOT RUN; they are run under AM1 and recorded, but this verdict stays FC. (2) The reading under AM1 (written after I4a failed, so a labelled post-hoc reading, not the committed one): the same function with I4a replaced by I4c and I4d, and with I2 not required (its remedy is the symmetrisation); I4b still failing makes FA impossible. It gives FA' never (I4b fails), FB' when I1, I3, I4c, I4d, I5, I6, E3a and E3d pass, SPLIT's Q rows do not all pass and some alternative passes whole (the recommended one the passing alternative with the fewest bytes), otherwise FC'. A decision to adopt any form rests on the committed verdict, and on (2) only as the measured evidence it is.
